chunks: Ali, from his father, from Safwan who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of a cow in the upper chest area. So he said: 'For the cow, the [correct method] is slaughter (dhabh), and what is done by nahr — that is not a valid slaughter (dhaki).'

key_terms.الذَّبْح: Dhabh — ritual slaughter by cutting the throat at the lower neck, the prescribed method for cattle and sheep
key_terms.الْمَنْحَر: Al-manhar — the upper chest/throat region, the site used for nahr (stabbing), prescribed for camels
key_terms.ذَكِيّ: Dhaki — ritually pure/valid slaughter that renders the animal permissible to eat
key_terms.نُحِرَ: Nahr — stabbing at the upper chest region, prescribed for camels, NOT for cows

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter a cow using the nahr method (stabbing the throat) in Islam?
ai.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) rules that for cattle (cows), the correct Islamic slaughter method is dhabh (cutting the throat at the lower neck), not nahr (stabbing at the upper chest/manhar). Using the nahr method for cows renders the meat impermissible. This distinction reflects classical Islamic jurisprudence: nahr is the designated method for camels, while dhabh is prescribed for cattle and sheep.
